findings.issue: `sc-ai jev ask` now discards a session-log flush failure with `let _ = finish_log(&prepared)`. Phase A reported it as an envelope warning (CR-014, status implemented). The ask envelope also lost `prompt_sha256`. The sprint's own rationale says 'no consumer behaviour changes beyond the pinned response shape'. No later sprint owns the restore: r-3b's `ask_from` returns a bare JudgeOutcome and only `run_from` appends the warning. No REQ text is violated, but a shipped hardening is silently regressed.
findings.required_correction: Choose one: (a) give ask a warnings slot (for example `Envelope::ask(..).with_warning(..)`, or an AskResponse type) and report the flush failure; or (b) record in r-3b and the ADR-SAG-0014 r-2 amendment that ask has no warning channel, and amend the CR-014 disposition row. In either case name the owning sprint. Do not leave the drop recorded only in this sprint's deviation table.

findings.issue: `discover_repo_root` maps every `Err(_)` from `discover_toplevel` (git missing, git failing, unreadable directory) to 'start'. D2.4 only specifies the outside-git case. A failing git inside a real repository therefore silently picks a subdirectory as the root, so a different .env is read and relative-path validation uses a different root. This is the same git-toplevel vs cwd disagreement D2.4 was meant to end.
findings.required_correction: Fall back only when git is absent (spawn NotFound) or reports 'not a git repository'. Map other errors to a typed error. Add a test for that case, and state the narrowed rule in the ADR-SAG-0003 r-2 amendment.

findings.issue: D2.9 says the facade lists exactly the items above, and the REQ-SAG-0620 row says the facade lists only prepare/run/discover_repo_root as run entry points. The boundary notes admit more public items, kept 'because crate tests import them': config::load_check_str, extract::extract_input, payload::build_payload, payload::parse_question_set, equal_input::producer_from_extractions, session::{StoredSession, SESSION_CONTEXT_HEADER, STALE_TMP_AGE}. `payload::build_payload` and `extract::extract_input` are a public second route to payload assembly, which cuts against ADR-SAG-0005 'facade owns payload assembly' and the 'one way to run' outcome. These widenings are not in the deviation table (only the OP_* and RunResponseBuilder additions are).

findings.issue: D11.3 says the ProducerError producer name comes 'from the input'. The implementation uses the file stem of argv[0]. For the common `python3 script.py` or `uv run ...` form this names the interpreter, not the producer.
findings.required_correction: Use an explicit optional `name` on the command input, falling back to the stem of the first non-interpreter argument or argv[0]. Otherwise document the interpreter limitation in REQ-SAG-0313's row or the extraction doc.

findings.issue: The amended REQ-SAG-0710 row says 'plus session_id' with no null case. ADR-SAG-0014 r-2 and ADR-SAG-0024 define session_id as null unless a session is saved, which is the Jev-only and dry-run behaviour. The requirement text under-describes the contract the code implements.
findings.required_correction: Reword the REQ-SAG-0710 amendment to 'session_id (null unless session_saved)'.

findings.issue: `Envelope::run` and `Envelope::ask` (public, infallible signatures) contain `panic!` paths in `to_object`. The `# Panics` rustdoc says they are unreachable. Library code in extract/command.rs also uses `.expect(...)` on the piped stderr handle. No REQ text forbids this, so it is only a robustness note. The key-order claim in the D2.6 body is also unproven: Envelope.data is a plain `serde_json::Map` with no preserve_order feature.
findings.required_correction: Prefer a fallible Envelope constructor, or `serde_json::value::to_raw_value`, so a public method cannot panic. Add a test that pins the printed key order, or relax the documented order claim to 'unordered object'.
